title: Speaking Practice - Helping Students Overcome Fear of Speaking English
subject: English Reading, Listening & Speaking
instructions:
Read the article 'Helping Students Overcome Fear of Speaking English' aloud, using a calm and encouraging voice. Pause after important points.
- Write the tough words from the module with their Hindi meanings.
- Write the key points of the article in your own hand.
- Record yourself reading the article aloud.
Submit a clear photo or PDF of your written page. If you also submit the recording, its transcript is produced outside the grading module before anything is marked.

rubric.name: Tough words and Hindi meanings
rubric.description: All 11 words in the approved sample module are expected. Each English word is written and paired with a correct Hindi meaning.

rubric.name: Key points recorded
rubric.description: The main points of the article are written out and match what the article actually says.

rubric.name: Spoken content coverage
rubric.description: Checks whether the locally produced transcript communicates the required article content and key ideas. Do not score accent, dialect, native-like pronunciation, tone, or speaking confidence. Minor grammar differences and likely Whisper recognition errors must not reduce marks when meaning is understandable; use uncertainty to lower confidence and route to educator review.

rubric.name: Required work completed
rubric.description: Every part of the task - the word list, the meanings, and the key points - is visibly attempted.

rubric.name: Legibility and organization
rubric.description: The page is readable and laid out clearly. Do not judge handwriting style or neatness as a personal quality.

title: Day 12 - 71-TS | Delegating Tasks - Time Management
subject: English Reading, Listening & Speaking
instructions:
Read aloud the complete article "Empowering the Classroom: The Strength of Delegating Tasks" from the approved Day 12 module.
- You may upload an existing video from your computer; recording inside the portal is optional.
- The locally hosted app saves the video locally and uses Whisper to create a transcript.
- Only the transcript is sent to the AI assessment agent for rubric-based feedback; raw video and audio are not sent.
- For written evidence, include the 15 tough words with Hindi meanings and the 10 simple sentences from the task.

rubric.name: Article coverage and reading accuracy
rubric.description: The locally produced transcript covers the supplied article and preserves its central statements about fair delegation, student responsibility, inclusion, teamwork, shared leadership, and time for individual support. Score only from transcript text.

rubric.name: Key ideas communicated
rubric.description: The submission communicates the article’s main ideas, including fair sharing of classroom responsibilities, confidence for quiet learners, teamwork, and more teacher time for learning support.

rubric.name: Tough vocabulary coverage
rubric.description: The submission includes or correctly uses the task vocabulary where relevant. For written evidence, check the 15 English words and Hindi meanings from the approved module; for video, use only words recognized in the transcript.

rubric.name: Required task completed
rubric.description: The submitted evidence completes the selected task format. A video submission must contain a usable local transcript; written work should include the requested vocabulary and simple sentences.

title: Project 01 - My Journey Begins
subject: Career Planning, AI & Communication
instructions:
Complete the My Journey project using the WES module.
1. Write about your dream: who you want to become, why, and what inspires you.
2. Create a two-year roadmap covering the first 3 months, the next two 4-month periods, and your goals for each year.
3. Explain how AI, computers, and technology can help you work toward your dream.
4. Explain how the Fellowship can help you improve skills, English, communication, confidence, discipline, and leadership.
5. Create a 5-7 slide presentation about your journey.
6. Prepare a 2-minute vision video introducing yourself, your dream, why you joined, what you hope to learn, and your commitment.
For the recommended portal test, combine your written work and exported presentation into one PDF. You can also test clear page photos or submit the vision video separately; local Whisper creates its transcript and raw video never enters the grading model.

rubric.name: Dream and inspiration
rubric.description: Clearly explains the learner's desired future, reasons for that goal, and sources of inspiration. Evaluate reflection and clarity, not the social value or prestige of the chosen dream.

rubric.name: Two-year roadmap
rubric.description: Provides a practical staged plan covering the first three months, the next two four-month periods, and intended yearly achievements.

rubric.name: AI and technology connection
rubric.description: Explains specific, realistic ways AI, computers, or technology could support the learner's goals while avoiding unsupported guarantees.

rubric.name: Fellowship development plan
rubric.description: Connects the Fellowship to growth in relevant areas such as skills, English, communication, confidence, discipline, and leadership.

rubric.name: Presentation completeness
rubric.description: The 5-7 slide presentation communicates the journey in a clear sequence and includes the required project components. Teacher review is required when slide evidence is unavailable.

rubric.name: Vision video reflection
rubric.description: The two-minute reflection addresses identity, dream, reason for joining, learning hopes, and personal commitment. Score only from a transcript produced outside the grading model; never infer personality, sincerity, or emotion from appearance or voice.
